title: Epilepsy, Parkinson's disease and multiple sclerosis
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's neurological condition.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for seizure disorder.

HPI
The patient is an 86-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up of his seizure disorder. He reports that his condition has been well-controlled over the last six months. He denies any recent episodes of tonic-clonic activity or focal awareness alterations. He reports consistent adherence to his prescribed levetiracetam and denies any significant side effects such as dizziness, somnolence, or mood changes. He notes that his sleep patterns remain regular and he feels generally well.

Review of Systems
The patient denies chest pain, shortness of breath, fever, chills, or joint pain. He denies any recent falls, visual changes, or numbness/tingling in his extremities. He denies any changes in appetite or bowel habits.

Social History
The patient lives at home with his wife. He is retired and spends most of his time gardening and watching television. He denies tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
His father had hypertension and his mother had type 2 diabetes.

Medication List
- Levetiracetam 500mg twice daily
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20mg daily

Vitals
Blood Pressure: 128/78 mmHg
Heart Rate: 72 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Temperature: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on room air
Weight: 175 lbs

Recent Labs
HbA1c: 5.8%
eGFR: 65 mL/min/1.73m2
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L
Sodium: 139 mEq/L
Potassium: 4.2 mEq/L

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. He appears in no acute distress. His speech is clear and coherent. Neurological exam reveals normal gait and steady balance. Cranial nerves II-XII are intact. Muscle strength is 5/5 throughout. Reflexes are 2+ and symmetric. No tremors or involuntary movements noted.

Assessment
1. Seizure disorder: The patient’s seizure disorder remains stable and well-controlled on his current dose of levetiracetam. He is currently asymptomatic.

Plan
1. Continue levetiracetam 500mg twice daily.
2. Continue current antihypertensive and lipid-lowering medications.
3. Follow up in 6 months for routine monitoring.

Electronically signed, P. O'Brien, PA-C, 05/14/2026
explanations: 'Seizure disorder' indexes to epilepsy, unspecified: G40.909 (HCC 201).

distractors.why: A seizure disorder is a diagnosis (G40.909), not the symptom R56.9.
